Leidos is focused on innovation and solving complex technical problems across infrastructure operations, cybersecurity analytics, and application modernization. The Cloud Infrastructure Engineer supports the operation, maintenance, automation, troubleshooting, security, and modernization of AWS and hybrid-cloud infrastructure for federal systems while developing expertise in cloud infrastructure, networking, automation, and security.
Electronics
Government
Information Technology
National Defense
Software
Computer
Information Services
National Security
H1B Sponsor Likely
Responsibilities
Support AWS infrastructure including EC2, S3, VPC, IAM, CloudWatch, Systems Manager, load balancing, DNS, and related services
Implement infrastructure changes using established architecture, procedures, and infrastructure-as-code
Maintain and modify Terraform and/or CloudFormation configurations under guidance from senior engineers
Monitor cloud resources and investigate availability, performance, configuration, and security issues
Troubleshoot networking, operating system, application connectivity, permissions, DNS, and cloud-service issues
Support vulnerability remediation, patching, configuration compliance, and security-hardening activities
Assist with cloud migrations, modernization efforts, disaster recovery, and infrastructure lifecycle activities
Develop scripts and automation to reduce repetitive administrative work
Maintain technical documentation, diagrams, procedures, and change records
Participate in incident response and root-cause analysis
Work with senior engineers to learn cloud architecture, security, networking, automation, and operational best practices
Gradually assume ownership of cloud services and technical workstreams as experience develops
Qualification

Self-initiative
Required
Bachelor's degree in information systems or relevant field and 1-3 years of practical experience in the field
Ability to obtain public trust clearance
Ability to independently manage assigned work, document technical activities, communicate issues, and seek assistance when appropriate
Demonstrated self-initiative to build enterprise-like AWS systems and resources that align with well-architected frameworks
Understanding of fundamental networking concepts including TCP/IP, DNS, routing, subnets, and firewalls/security groups, with the ability to apply systematic troubleshooting methods
Basic understanding of infrastructure security concepts such as least privilege, vulnerability remediation, system hardening, and security baselines
Hands-on experience building solutions with Cloudformation, Terraform, Python, or other tools
Preferred
Cloud related certifications (Solutions Architect, Azure Administrator, etc)
Exposure to CIS Benchmarks, STIGs, or similar security and compliance frameworks
